itens.titulo: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos
itens.descricao: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos CNBC
trechos: "That risk is real risk, and that's why when the frontier-type models came out.
… A lot of us sat down and said, 'How do we figure out how to get through this quickly?" Moynihan told CNBC's Leslie Picker.
"We put on 1,000 contractors to help us do the patching work in the second quarter, and those people remain here today, helping us, on top of the 3,000 people we have in that area," he said.

The bank spent a "couple hundred million plus" on the software remediation and regulatory issues related to anti-money laundering compliance in the third quarter, Moynihan told analysts earlier Wednesday.
"We've got to stay ahead of them, and we've got to be mindful that the people doing the software development are the people trying to sell us the services," Moynihan said.
Still, Moynihan — speaking as his company's shares slumped as much as 8% Wednesday — sought to reassure investors that the spending increase was temporary.
"Once you patch, you don't have to patch as much.
… The pipeline moves through," Moynihan said, adding that the bank expects remediation costs to decline over time.

itens.titulo: Why Bank of America (BAC) Shares Are Trading Lower Today
itens.descricao: Why Bank of America (BAC) Shares Are Trading Lower Today Yahoo Finance
trechos: Shares of financial services giant Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) fell 7.4% in the pre-market session after the company reported third-quarter earnings per share that missed analyst consensus estimates amid a $1.2 billion anti-money-laundering penalty.
According to a company press release, Bank of America reported third-quarter earnings per share of $0.91.
That result fell short of the analyst consensus estimate of $1.10 per share.
The topline also fell short with total revenue clocking in at $29.96 billion vs analyst estimates of $30.56 billion (2.6% year-on-year growth, 2% miss).Compounding the earnings miss, The U.S.

Department of the Treasury announced enforcement actions totaling more than $1.21 billion against the lender for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, with FinCEN assessing a $1.2 billion penalty.
The bank disclosed in its press release that this non-tax-deductible civil penalty added $1.2 billion to noninterest expense, reducing EPS by $0.17.

Excluding the charge, adjusted EPS was $1.08, indicating the penalty drove almost the entire $0.19 bottom-line miss.Operationally, net interest income increased 8% to $16.45 billion on loan and deposit growth and fixed-rate asset repricing, the company said.
That core expansion helped offset top-line headwinds from an 11% decline in investment banking fees to $1.8 billion and a 5% drop in sales and trading revenue to $5.1 billion.
